input: Research local fostering options for a senior cat

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether the goal is to foster OUT a senior cat the user owns, or to find a foster placement to TAKE IN a senior cat changes the entire research direction.
Geographic location determines which shelters, rescues, and programs are actually reachable and relevant.
The cat's specific medical or behavioral needs (e.g., chronic illness, mobility issues) will filter which foster programs or hosts are equipped to help.
Knowing whether this is for the user's own cat vs. a stray or a cat belonging to someone else affects who needs to be contacted and what agreements are required.
Whether the user wants a temporary foster arrangement or a permanent foster-to-adopt setup changes which programs to prioritize.
Some people prefer shelter-run programs, others want independent foster networks or breed-specific rescues — this shapes where to look first.
Knowing what a good outcome looks like (e.g., a vetted list of contacts, a chosen organization, an application submitted) defines when the research is actually done.

gold.taskTitle: Research local fostering options for a senior cat
gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate local organizations or individuals that offer fostering arrangements specifically suited to a senior cat.

questions.title: Are you placing your cat into foster care, or taking one in?
questions.description: Clarify the direction of the fostering arrangement — whether the user needs to find a foster home for a cat they own, or wants to become a foster carer for a senior cat themselves.

questions.title: What city or region should the search focus on?
questions.description: Identify the user's geographic location to narrow results to locally relevant shelters, rescues, and foster networks.

questions.title: Does the cat have any medical or special care needs?
questions.description: Determine if the senior cat has conditions like kidney disease, hyperthyroidism, or mobility issues that require a foster program with veterinary support.

questions.title: Is this cat yours, a stray, or someone else's?
questions.description: Establish ownership and responsibility so the right contacts, consent, and agreements can be identified from the start.

questions.title: Is the foster arrangement meant to be temporary or long-term?
questions.description: Distinguish between a short-term foster stay and a permanent foster-to-adopt placement to target the appropriate programs.

questions.title: Do you prefer a shelter program, rescue group, or private network?
questions.description: Understand the user's preference for the type of organization to guide whether to look at municipal shelters, breed-specific rescues, or community foster platforms.

questions.title: What does a successful research outcome look like to you?
questions.description: Define the end goal — whether that means a shortlist of contacts, a submitted application, or a confirmed foster match — so the plan has a clear finish line.
